column1: # Preregistered trailing-fill print predictions (TrailingTruth), locked before the fresh Arial 60% export.
# Fixture: tools/excel-parity/make-print-numfill-fixture.py --set trail-holdout
#   workbook tests/test-documents-excel/synthetic-print-numfill-trail-holdout.xlsx
#   manifest tools/excel-parity/print-numfill-trail-holdout-cells.tsv
#   face/scale Arial 11 pt at 60 % (fresh face and fresh print scale; training used Aptos Narrow 14 at 100 %)
# Formats: N1 `0.00` control, S2 `0.00* ` (space suffix), D2 `0.00*.` (dot suffix),
#          F8 `0.00*-;0.00` (dash suffix on positive/zero; second section `0.00` on negative).
# Widths 5.5..12.0 in 0.25-char steps, four bands, left/centre/right sheets, values +1234.5/-1234.5/0.
# Measurement: measure-print-numfill.py content-stream Tm/TJ positions. Fill counts are counted in
# emitted text order after the matched amount, so a first fill glyph whose origin sits a few
# hundredths before the number's /Widths advance end is still counted (the old x-threshold count
# dropped it: 8 emitted spaces were counted as 7). Cell edges are printed border centrelines.
# Training truth (Aptos Narrow 14 / 100 %, direct Excel 2019, /var/tmp/numfill-oracle/trail-train):
#   972 cells measured, 0 monotonicity/step violations, 0 hash-vs-control mismatches, 0 sign mismatches.
#   Left: amount x0/x1 identical to the N1 twin for every fill count (max delta 0.000 pt).
#   Adv measured vs 600-dpi font model: space 2.626 vs 2.640, dot 3.594..3.650 vs 3.600,
#   Count law on all 140 left-aligned fill cells is exact with
#   N = floor((W_cell - pad - w(number)) / a), pad in [4.22, 4.32] pt (mid 4.27).
#   Excel quirk locked here: a multi-section format prints the negative section on the absolute
#   value, so F8's negative `0.00` prints "1234.50" with NO minus and no fill; its fit/hash control
#   is the positive N1 cell, not the negative one.
# The checks below are Excel-truth relations. excel_failures must be 0; ours_failures count the
# engine on the same relations. TOL = 0.35 pt unless a row says otherwise.
